title: Redwood migration demo - parity mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together
summary: 30-minute migration/product demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Covered API parameter mapping, streaming & function-calling differences, Console, Optimize recommendations, and security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs and dedicated vs hosted. Agreed next steps: share parity mapping doc, run benchmark with their prompt set, provide SOC2 + network diagram, schedule technical deep dive for infra team.

transcript:
Header: 2026-09-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Helix Head of ML), Marcus Liu (Helix Platform Eng), Tara Gomez (Helix Security), Ben Ortiz (Helix Legal)

Auto-generated Summary: demo focused on mapping parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API; security brief; next steps to benchmark and share docs.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, this is Diego and Ravi on the engineering side. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Asha Patel: Doing good, thanks Lena. We're excited - we have a pretty manual migration plan and want to see where Redwood maps to our current OpenAI/Anthropic stack.
[00:15] Marcus Liu: Quick note, we care mostly about latency for live product features and cost for batch embeddings. Also security and VPC or private deployment options.
[00:25] Lena: Great, we'll cover API parity first, then Console and Optimize, and finish with security and pilot plan. Feel free to interrupt.

[00:40] Diego Ramos: Ok jumping in - on the API side Redwood supports text generation, chat, embeddings, rerank. For parity mapping, most OpenAI/Anthropic params line up: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences. One difference: Redwood's streaming semantics include chunked token frames and we support tool/function calls with structured JSON returns.
[01:05] Asha: When you say "tool calls" do you mean the same as OpenAI function calling? How close is the match?
[01:12] Diego: It's similar but with slight differences. Redwood supports the same concept - you provide a schema, the model returns a call, but the call payload and error-handling differ a bit. We include explicit call-id and have stronger retry semantics on transport-level disconnects. In practice, code changes are limited to adapting the response wrapper.
[01:38] Marcus: Any sample SDK snippets? We use Python and Go.
[01:42] Ravi Shah: Yes, we'll send SDK snippets. For Python it's 2-3 lines to switch: client = Redwood(api_key) and the call shape mirrors OpenAI's chat completion but the field names are consistent across hosted/dedicated/private.

[02:05] Lena: On embeddings, we've seen parity with OpenAI embeddings in terms of API shape - but we offer additional controls around batching and cache TTLs so you can dedupe and reduce calls. For Together embeddings we map similarly though some tokenization differences might change nearest-neighbor results slightly.
[02:30] Asha: That's a big concern for us: our similarity search is sensitive. How much work to reproduce current vectors?
[02:36] Diego: Two options - 1) run a one-time re-embed with Redwood and compare cosine similarity; 2) enable hybrid caching and shadowing, Redwood can serve requests to both backends and we measure drift. We'll help run the benchmark.

[03:00] Marcus: Latency - you mentioned dedicated vs hosted. Our SLA requirement is 300ms p95 on short chat messages. Can Redwood hit that?
[03:08] Diego: For short sequences and small models yes; for larger gen models p95 could be higher. With Dedicated and pinned model variants we can get predictable latency. Also the runtime has KV caching for prefixes which reduces p95 for repeated contexts.
[03:25] Tara Gomez: Security: we need SOC2 and SAML/SSO, plus KMS integration and audit logs. Any network diagrams?
[03:33] Lena: We can provide SOC2, and we support SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. We'll attach the SOC2 and a sample network diagram. For hosted customers we offer VPC peering and private link options.

[03:50] Ben Ortiz: On legal, data retention and deletion policies are important. Can you sign a DPA?
[03:56] Lena: Yes, we have a DPA template and can negotiate terms. We'll have legal follow up.

[04:10] Diego: Back to parity specifics - a few non-obvious mapping notes: OpenAI's "presence_penalty" maps to Redwood's "bias_presence" in the SDK; "frequency_penalty" maps to "bias_frequency". Also temperature semantics are identical but Redwood exposes an extra "determinism" flag for model variants tuned for low randomness which helps in regen-heavy pipelines.
[04:40] Asha: Those name differences are annoying but ok if mapped. Can you give the spreadsheet?
[04:44] Lena: We'll share a parity mapping spreadsheet with exact field pairs and sample requests.

[05:00] Diego: Functionally, for Anthropic-style assistant/chat-> Redwood mapping, we preserve the role/message structure, but we recommend normalizing system prompts since token counting differs slightly. Together AI sometimes uses different tokenization causing max_tokens behavior to shift; we add a conservative fudge factor recommendation in the sheet.

[06:00] Marcus: Cost - do you have rough unit economics? We're currently at $0.0005/token with our current provider for small models.
[06:07] Lena: Pricing depends on model and deployment; hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved. Redwood Optimize will analyze your workload and recommend model+quantization combos to meet latency and cost targets. We'll run Optimize on your prompt set during the pilot.

[06:35] Ravi: Demo time - opening the Redwood Console. You'll see per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and a model catalog with verified profiles.
[06:45] Asha: Oh you have a verified perf profile - that's helpful.
[06:48] Diego: Yes, we include benchmarks (throughput, latency, memory) for each model variant and quantization profile. In the Console you can pin model versions and set rollout policies (canary/A-B).

[07:10] Diego: Quick demo of a streaming chat - note how the stream frames show partial JSON in function calls; we include the call metadata so your app knows when to commit the action.
[07:28] Marcus: How do you handle reconnects mid-stream? We sometimes see mobile flakiness.
[07:33] Ravi: We have client-side reconnect logic and server-side resume tokens so the KV cache and stream offset sync; reconnects re-request missing segments and we attempt to diff, this reduces duplicate tokens.

[08:00] Asha: Embeddings pipeline - show batching config.
[08:04] Diego: In Optimize, you can set ideal batch sizes and TTL for prefix cache; Optimize suggests quantization level (e.g., int8 vs int4) for your accuracy targets. For your large-batch offline jobs, quantization + batching reduces cost by 3-5x in our experience.
[08:25] Tara: Any red flags on accuracy with int4?
[08:28] Diego: For embeddings int4 usually holds up; for some open models it can cause slight degradation. Optimize runs a quick eval and gives a quality delta so you can decide.

[09:00] Lena: Let's talk pilot plan - we'll provision a trial project, run a 1k-prompt benchmark, and do a side-by-side compare for latency, cost, and vector drift. We'll also do a security packet.
[09:12] Marcus: Sounds good. Timeline?
[09:15] Lena: We aim to deliver parity mapping + initial benchmark within two weeks. After bench we can scope Dedicated if results meet your thresholds.

[09:30] Asha: One more question - are there any breaking changes to prompt engineering when switching?
[09:33] Diego: Mostly wording around system prompts and stop sequences; also temperature/determinism interplay. We'll include recommended prompt changes in the mapping doc.

[10:00] Ben Ortiz: Legal follow-up on data flow - will you send a network diagram showing VPC peering?
[10:04] Lena: Yes, we'll attach a network diagram and DPA.

[10:20] Tara: About KMS, we need to know key lifecycle and whether Redwood stores any plaintext.
[10:24] Ravi: For Private deployments you control the KMS; in Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and we do not persist plaintext for configured flows; we'll include specifics in the security packet.

[10:45] Asha: Let's try a quick live migration of a single chat path - can you show how we'd change a simple OpenAI chat call to Redwood?
[10:50] Diego: Sure, example: OpenAI chatCompletion with messages -> Redwood.chat.create with identical messages but replace presence_penalty with bias_presence and enable stream: true; I'll paste code in chat.
[11:10] (diego pastes code)
[11:15] Asha: Looks straightforward. Any gotchas?
[11:18] Diego: Watch for model name differences and token budget. Also Together's max tokens handling - if you used token_soft_limit you might need to switch to Redwood's explicit max_token cap.

[11:45] Marcus: How do we handle fallbacks across providers? We sometimes failover between providers to control cost.
[11:51] Diego: Redwood has smart routing - you can route by latency, cost, or region. We also support automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant or a different region. This is configured in the route policy.

[12:10] Lena: Ok quick recap: we'll send parity mapping sheet, SDK snippets, SOC2/network diagrams, provision trial keys, run benchmark and schedule technical deep dive.
[12:22] Asha: Perfect. Marcus and Tara will prep a list of infra and security questions.
[12:28] Ben Ortiz: Legal will follow up on the DPA.
[12:30] Lena: Awesome - thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invites.

Note: transcription contains occasional speaker attribution uncertainty and minor transcript errors typical of automated calls.
